Before departure, careful habits for cooling checks
This page helps new colleagues see what to do first

The Companion Animal Travel Desk keeps pet moves calm, safe, and clear. Good first checks prevent stress for the animal and save time for the team. Start by reading the booking notes, then confirm the crate, water plan, and fit for the cabin. Keep your wording simple with travelers, and never rush the handoff.

When you speak with the welcome team, stay steady and practical. <<FACT F041>> Ask for any special handling notes, and make sure the records stay aligned before boarding begins. If a pet seems uneasy, slow the pace and use a softer tone.

For onboard coordination, keep the route notes handy. <<FACT F051>> Share only what the crew needs, and pass along any health or comfort updates without delay. If another desk asks about space or placement, answer in plain language and check the file.

Some services use a named pet area, so match the label carefully. <<FACT F043>> Remember the key habit: check, confirm, and pass along only clear information.
